title: GitHub database failover after network partition
alert: A network partition occurred during GitHub data-center maintenance, followed by inconsistent website metadata and a lengthy recovery. Investigate the incident and identify the integrity-preserving response.

evidence.text: During scheduled replacement of 100G optical equipment, a network partition disrupted connectivity between GitHub East Coast sites.
Orchestrator quorum selected West Coast database primaries; recovered connectivity then exposed writes unique to each site.
Website metadata such as issues and pull requests could be stale or inconsistent; Git repository data was not lost.
GitHub paused webhook events and other internal processing while ensuring data integrity.
Immediate failback to the East Coast was unsafe because both regions held divergent writes.
The incident required extensive recovery and reconciliation of MySQL replication and background processing.

impact_options.name: GitHub website metadata such as issues and pull requests

root_hypotheses.description: The network partition triggered MySQL failover, leading to divergent write histories that could not safely fail back
A global Git repository storage deletion
A WAF regex exhausted HTTP CPU worldwide
A customer DNS misconfiguration affecting only one domain

response_options.description: Prioritize data integrity, pause background processing, reconcile replication and recover without unsafe failback
Force primary failback immediately despite divergent writes
Purge every Git repository as a precaution
Disable all TLS validation for cross-site replication

dataset_origin: Published first-party incident postmortem; curated and paraphrased source facts (NOT original telemetry)
